steps: Service A commits local state and publishes an outcome event.
The event bus delivers it to interested services.
Service B reacts, commits its own step, and emits the next event.
Service C completes or emits failure that triggers compensating reactions.

lesson.scenario: A farm-box subscription activates through domain events without a central workflow owner.

steps.title: Commit the subscription
steps.narration: The subscription ledger creates SUB-31 and emits a fact after its local commit.
steps.outcome: No coordinator tells downstream owners what to do.
steps.invariant: An event describes a committed fact, not a request for an uncommitted change.

steps.title: Allocate produce reactively
steps.narration: Harvest consumes SubscriptionStarted and commits crate C-88 for SUB-31.
steps.outcome: Harvest advances the workflow using only the event contract.
steps.invariant: Consumers deduplicate by event identity before committing local effects.

steps.title: Schedule delivery
steps.narration: Courier reacts to CrateAllocated and reserves stop D-14.
steps.outcome: The global path emerges from subscriptions rather than one visible state machine.
steps.invariant: Every event handler commits locally before publishing its successor fact.

steps.title: Charge after scheduling
steps.narration: Billing consumes DeliveryScheduled and captures the weekly fee.
steps.outcome: SUB-31 is operational across four autonomous owners.
steps.invariant: Event ordering for SUB-31 is preserved by its stream key.

steps.title: Ignore duplicate delivery
steps.narration: A redelivered DeliveryScheduled event is recognized by its event ID and does not charge twice.
steps.outcome: At-least-once delivery does not create a second $24 charge.
steps.invariant: Each subscriber owns durable idempotency for the events it consumes.
